analysis.title: Who really wins from AI? Ask India
key_insights: Deutsche Bank argues India may win from AI by adopting it at scale rather than building frontier models, using an infrastructure-light approach on top of existing national digital systems.
India's low correlation with global indices is now acting as a diversifier from AI volatility. Foreign institutions bought a record $9.5bn of Indian stocks in November.

India ranks No. 3 in the Stanford HAI Global AI Vibrancy Tool, behind the US and China, on R&D and talent. It ranks No. 1 in AI trust and regular intentional use at work (University of Melbourne/KPMG).
India became ChatGPT's largest market by weekly users. Altman said the number of users has doubled since the start of the year, helped by ads and low pricing (under $5 a month for many customers).

Bull case: 1.5bn potential adopters, existing digital public infrastructure (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, mobile, UPI), large unmet needs in healthcare, education, credit and agriculture, a large tech workforce, supportive government policy, and the ability to buy models rather than build them.
India's non-aligned position may let it extract favorable terms from both the US and China. Spending by US and Chinese labs to cut the cost of intelligence may transfer consumer surplus to India.

Bear case 1: AI could erode India's services advantage (about 40% of global business-process sourcing). DB's base case is that these fears are overdone. The tech industry employs about 5.8m people (under 1% of the workforce), and active tech openings hit a record 130,000, up 27% y/y (Xpheno).
Nasscom expects a 12-18 month transition phase of muted growth in IT and BPM services as providers shift to AI-enabled offerings.

Bear case 2: high usage may not translate into productivity. Only 23% of surveyed formal firms use AI (sophistication-adjusted) versus 43% in the US, and only 43% of graduates assessed by Mercer are immediately job-ready.

Bear case 3: power, compute and capital are binding constraints. The Ministry of Power nearly doubled its projected AI data-centre load to over 26 GW by 2031-32, about 7% of peak demand. India has under 0.5% of global GPU cluster performance, and its AI infrastructure investment depends heavily on imports.

Bear case 4: regulation and public opposition. India ranks 64th of 200+ economies on government effectiveness, data-centre policy is fragmented across states, protests have begun in Mumbai and Visakhapatnam, and 54% of Indians favour regulation that protects industries.

Data-centre vacancy is a record-low 2.8% (JLL). India's data-centre capacity is set to triple from 1.6 GW to 6 GW by 2029, and hyperscalers and neoclouds will build about 1.3 GW of the 4.4 GW in new capacity.

Investment commitments: Reliance about $110bn over seven years, Adani $100bn by 2035, and Tata-OpenAI 100 MW (option for 1 GW). Amazon ($35bn), Microsoft ($17.5bn) and Google ($15bn) account for $67.5bn of foreign commitments.
Short-term, the 'anti-AI trade' has reversed. From Oct 7 to Nov 18 the Nifty 50 rose about 12% and the Nifty IT rose 13%, while the S&P 500 fell 6.1%, the Nasdaq 11% and the Kospi about 25%.

Year to Oct 7, the Nifty 50 fell 14% and the Nifty IT fell 27%, while the S&P 500 gained 14%, the Nasdaq 18% and the Kospi 58%. Foreign investors sold a net $26bn of Indian equities in the first nine months of the year.
One-year correlation of the Nifty IT with the Nasdaq, Kospi and S&P 500 is near zero. One-month correlation is about -0.4 to -0.5. The Nifty 50 has a one-year correlation of +0.1 to +0.3.

Valuations: Nifty IT trades at 19x earnings versus the Nasdaq at nearly 40x. The Nifty 50 trades at 22x (peak of 34x five years ago) and the S&P 500 at 23x. Further Indian gains likely need earnings growth.

Risks to the hedge: weaker IT exports and dollar earnings colliding with an import-heavy capex cycle could pressure the current account, and the hedge may fade if AI sentiment turns consistently positive.

Long-term beneficiaries by DB's framework: AI infrastructure (limited domestic upside unless India builds capacity), IT services (partner or disrupted), and adopters (banks and insurers, consumer discretionary, healthcare, agriculture).

sector_views.rationale: May benefit as AI partners and implementers but carry disruption risk. The top eight Indian listed tech companies are all IT services firms, and investors question AI disintermediation.
Listed among adopters with the largest pool of expensive challenges to apply cheap AI to, such as micro-credit scoring and collections.
Listed among the adopters expected to benefit most from cheap AI applied to costly challenges.
AI diagnostics and telemedicine could reach the two thirds of the population who currently lack specialist care.

sector_views.sector: India AI infrastructure (data centres, power, cabling)
sector_views.rationale: Dominated by international companies, so upside for India is limited unless domestic capacity is built. Cooling and automation come almost entirely from overseas suppliers.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Outpaces advanced economies at 2.1% and 1.8%, and China at 4.5% and 4%.

macro_indicators.reading: Telecom, computer and information services exports up about 13% to more than $200bn, about 5% of the $4trn economy
macro_indicators.interpretation: Shows the economic weight of the IT sector, which is exposed to AI disruption risk.
Supports the view that services exports have been growing despite AI fears so far.

macro_indicators.reading: More than 26 GW by 2031-2032, about 7% of total peak power demand
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Ministry of Power nearly doubled its earlier projection, which raises grid strain risk.
JLL projects Asia's fastest-growing digital infrastructure market.
Record level, which contradicts the view that AI is cutting tech hiring (Xpheno).

risk_factors: AI automates India's outsourcing and services labour, hitting its main competitive advantage.
High AI usage may not convert into productivity because of uneven adoption, skills gaps and the lack of organisational change.
Power grid strain, imported hardware dependence, component shortages and a possible data-centre overcapacity glut by the end of the decade.
Limited capital: private AI investment in India was about $4bn last year against $12bn in China and over $285bn in the US.
Fragmented state-level data-centre policy, public protests over water and electricity use, and a public that favours protective regulation.
Weaker IT exports and dollar earnings combined with an import-heavy capex cycle could pressure the current account.
Rotation reverses if AI sentiment turns positive again, ending the diversifier appeal of Indian equities.
Elevated Indian valuations mean further equity gains likely require earnings growth.
charts_described: Figure 1 shows foreign institutions investing record amounts in Indian stocks in November (USDbn, monthly).
Figure 18 compares stock index performance for 2026 YTD and Oct 1 to Nov 18, per the text: the S&P 500 -6.1%, Nasdaq -11% and Kospi about -25% since Oct 7, while the Nifty 50 rose about 12%.
vol_and_positioning: Foreign institutions bought a record $9.5bn of Indian stocks in November, after net selling of $26bn in the first nine months of the year.
One-month correlation of the Nifty IT with the Nasdaq, Kospi and S&P 500 is about -0.4 to -0.5, and the one-year correlation is near zero.
The 'anti-AI' hedge may run out if AI sentiment turns consistently positive or if AI regulation and geopolitical concerns in the US subside.
geopolitical: US and China are competing for AI leadership. Trump is quoted saying 'Whoever wins AI, wins'.
Rising tensions may force countries to pick a side if the US cuts off chip supplies or China stops shipping rare earth metals. DB says non-aligned India is best placed to extract terms from both.
The US announced it would suspend eight tech companies, including Microsoft, Infosys and TCS, from a green card programme dominated by Indian employees.
The US has shown it can ban the use of a model without warning, which raises the risk of dependence on one model or country.
Data localisation measures from 2000 to 2024: East Asia and Pacific 77, Europe and Central Asia 66, South Asia 24, North America 3.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech employs only about 5.8m people (under 1% of workforce). Active openings hit a record 130,000 (+27% y/y). Nasscom expects AI to raise demand for outsourced integration, orchestration and governance. An ICRIER survey of about 650 IT firms found no evidence of large-scale job losses.
tension_points.bear_case: Generative AI is most likely to automate the cheap educated labour behind India's outsourcing model (customer support, junior coding, back-office GCC work). Entry-level hiring may dry up, and Nifty IT employment has flatlined since early 2023.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nasscom expects a 12-18 month transition of muted growth for providers. A longer or deeper slowdown in IT and GCC export growth would weaken the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Low correlation with the Nasdaq, Kospi and S&P 500, record foreign inflows of $9.5bn in November, and lower P/E multiples (Nifty IT at 19x versus the Nasdaq at nearly 40x).
tension_points.bear_case: Indian multiples are still high, so further gains need earnings growth. Weaker IT exports and dollar earnings could collide with an import-heavy capex cycle and pressure the current account.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The hedge may run out if sentiment around AI becomes consistently positive again, or if concerns about US AI regulation and great-power tensions subside.

theme_stances.key_argument: India's minimal direct AI exposure has turned from a weakness into a short-term diversifier as global AI stocks sell off.
theme_stances.evidence: Indian stocks have bucked the global selloff

theme_stances.key_argument: India can benefit by adopting AI at scale on existing digital infrastructure without building frontier models.
theme_stances.evidence: nowhere else has AI operating leverage like India

theme_stances.key_argument: DB's base case is that fears of AI disrupting Indian IT services look overdone, but a 12-18 month transition of muted growth is expected.
theme_stances.evidence: Our base case though is that these fears look overdone.
